text:
maria: noticing a weird perf blip on prod-rt earlier, pages had higher p95 and GPU utilization spiked
kevin: saw the same, started ~08:10 UTC, p95 doubled for short requests
sam: cache-proxy error rate jumped at that time, 503s from backend proxy queueing
elaine: any recent changes to keying or prefetch?
maria: deployed small tokenizer-normalize tweak 07:45 by @kevin, supposed to trim trailing whitespace consistently
kevin: yep, that change added a normalization step that accidentally preserved a random nonce suffix for some prompts (regex bug)
sam: result was higher cache key cardinality -> almost zero hit-rate for those prefixes. backend saw an on-demand miss spike and kernel selector started falling back
maria: kernel selector logs: "no compat kernel for optimized-path, falling back to int8-gemm" which increased per-token latency 2x-3x
elaine: prefetch-bot: prefetching paused due to cache miss storm, refill rate couldn't keep up :warning:
prefetch-bot: action: scaled prefetch workers x2 at 08:18, then drained because backend throttle hit
kevin: rolling back normalization now, will flip feature flag to restore canonical keying
deploy-bot: rollout-started by kevin: feature_flag=tokenizer_normalize -> OFF
maria: rolling back reduced miss-rate slowly, but kernel selector still observed degraded distribution because warm KV cache wasn't populated
sam: mitigated by temporarily enabling prefix-serve throttle: added 150rps cap to miss-to-backend to stop overload (applied to cache-proxy)
kevin: command used: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.internal/flags/tokenizer_normalize/off`
elaine: also adjusted batching heuristics to prefer small latency-sensitive batches while cache re-warms (policy: prefer_max_latency=20ms)
maria: after rollback + throttle + batch tweak, p95 recovered to baseline around 08:50 UTC
kevin: root cause = key-normalization regression: preserved ephemeral nonce for ~0.6% of requests but those were common prefixes -> catastrophic effect on hit-rate
sam: follow-ups: add keying fuzz tests and canary on production traffic subset, add metric for "key-cardinality-change" to alert on >10% jump in 5m window
elaine: runtime follow-ups: kernel-selector should have better guard: if fallback kernel increases p95 > 1.5x, route to compatible model variant or return degraded-mode instead of saturating backend
maria: ops checklist: (1) revert change (done), (2) throttle misses (done), (3) warm-up prefetch with prioritized queues (in progress), (4) add post-deploy sanity that validates hit-rate delta < 5%
kevin: will open a PR with normalization fix + unit tests and add canary rollout plan (owner: kevin)
sam: I'll add cache-proxy rate-limiter and a circuit-breaker to avoid backend overload next time (owner: sam)
elaine: I'll write the follow-up in incidents/ and schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow. link: <https://redwood-internal/incident/1912478910> :spiral_note_pad:
maria: thanks everyone, big win getting it stable quickly. We'll keep the incident thread updated with PMs and timelines
kevin: one more note — profiling showed kernel-selector re-evaluations were O(n) in compatible-kernel set; I'll optimize that path to avoid CPU spikes during miss storms
maria: closing actions: owners assigned, patch + canary, add alerting. leaving this thread open for notes. :thumbsup:
